title: CYBRIK receipt trust-bundle and durability design packet
description: PROPOSED — NOT ACCEPTED — NOT IMPLEMENTED. This packet proposes public receipt-verification trust-bundle lifecycle semantics and cross-product observable durable-commit ordering. It selects no signer, key store, distribution system, ledger, database, server, deployment or production configuration.

design_invariants.rule: Trust-bundle generation increases monotonically and names its immediate predecessor when present.
Every successor retains every predecessor kid; keys leave signing service by state change, never deletion.
State moves active to retiring to retired, or any state to revoked, and never backwards.
Revocation is retained as a positive fact with time, reason and prospective or retroactive verifier effect.
At most one key is active for the receipt-signer role in one generation.
A verifier uses only locally distributed public bundles and fails closed when missing or stale; bundle_uri is never fetched.
Bundles contain public OKP Ed25519 material only and kid equals the RFC 7638 unpadded base64url thumbprint.
An authoritative invocation intent is durably committed before dispatch.
The signed completion receipt is durably committed and read-after-write verified before a result is released.
Failure to durably commit a required receipt never maps to completed and exposes no receipt_id or business output.
Unresolved intents terminalize to failed or timed-out receipts, and performed-unrecorded outcomes are alarm-grade reconciliation states that never map to completed.
Application runtime cannot update or delete a committed receipt; correction requires a future versioned supersession design.
Only durable receipts are readable; unavailable does not distinguish never-created from not-yet-durable.
Receipt retention never exceeds retention of trust-bundle generations needed to verify it.
An idempotent replay returns the exact stored receipt and never signs again.

authority_boundaries.trust_bundle_fetch: offline local bundle only; bundle_uri is never a fetch instruction
authority_boundaries.signing: Fabric control plane only; never executor, SOC, Cyber AI, model or agent
authority_boundaries.distribution: Fabric-owned product and operations decision constrained by this public-bundle contract

durable_receipt_semantics: commit and read-after-write verify signed receipt before releasing completed result
return stored receipt bytes on replay
preserve failed uncertain commits for reconciliation without repeating execution

retention_coupling.note: Values are bounded non-production design fixtures, not production retention policy.

ownership.suite: cross-product contracts and static evidence only
ownership.fabric: signer, trust distribution, durable ledger and runtime authority
ownership.soc: alert, case, analyst and tenant truth only

open_product_decisions: Fabric selects the production HSM or KMS, signing authorization policy and key ceremony.
Fabric selects bundle distribution mechanism, freshness operating value and compromise runbook.
Fabric selects ledger engine, replication, backup, RPO, RTO and retention policy.
A separately versioned contract is required before receipt correction or supersession.

validator_dependencies.resolution_order: repository-local first; explicit CYBRIK_CONTRACT_VALIDATION_DEPS_ROOT override second
validator_dependencies.external_root_policy: allowed only when exact package versions match the lockfile-pinned validator toolchain

verification.scope: Static packet integrity and named fixture semantics only; no runtime, signer, distribution or ledger behavior is proven.
